task.title: Prepare selected skill instructions as inert artifacts
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/652 by preparing exact selected skill entrypoints as bounded immutable UTF-8 instructions without granting prompt or execution authority.
acceptance_criteria: Reject non-skill selections before filesystem access and preserve deterministic exact-ID ordering.
Revalidate package, manifest, entrypoint, and descriptor identity through the shared descriptor-anchored preparation boundary.
Enforce a 1 MiB plus probe-byte read boundary, valid UTF-8, all-or-nothing failure, and redacted diagnostics.
Keep prepared instructions inert with no registration, provider composition, execution, persistence, workflow activation, or tool grant.

attempts.summary: Established RED integration coverage for bounded exact-content skill preparation.
attempts.diagnostic: The focused skill_preparation test initially failed to compile because no prepared-skill artifact or skill preparation API existed.
attempts.patch: Added coverage for exact content and order, wrong-kind preflight, empty selection, size boundaries, invalid UTF-8, changed identities, unsafe symlinks, and all-or-nothing failure.

attempts.summary: Implemented skill preparation by sharing the descriptor-anchored byte boundary.
attempts.diagnostic: Reusing the existing bounded raw-byte preparation path kept filesystem identity checks DRY while a skill-specific conversion layer enforced UTF-8 and preserved inert semantics.
attempts.patch: Added PreparedSkillArtifact, typed preparation failures, the 1 MiB skill limit, exact-kind selection, documentation, and ADR-0004.

attempts.summary: Removed content disclosure and corrected generalized diagnostics during review.
attempts.diagnostic: Independent review found that derived Debug output exposed authored instructions; substantive review also found an expected-kind diagnostic still hardcoded to Tool and an avoidable UTF-8 buffer copy.
attempts.patch: Redacted prepared instruction Debug output, derived mismatch text from the stored expected kind, converted owned bytes with String::from_utf8, and added regression coverage.

outcome.summary: Selected skill entrypoints now become exact, bounded, UTF-8, descriptor-revalidated artifacts that remain inert until a later caller-owned registration and composition boundary.

verification.command: GitHub Rust quality gate https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/actions/runs/30263008181 and substantive exact-head CodeRabbit review at https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/pull/653

lessons: Instruction text is sensitive authored content even when it is inert, so diagnostics and Debug implementations must redact it by construction.
Sharing byte-level descriptor revalidation avoids duplicating filesystem trust logic while allowing skill-specific encoding and size policy.
A generalized helper must derive diagnostics from its stored expected kind rather than retain tool-specific wording.
Owned UTF-8 conversion can validate and reuse the existing buffer without copying the full instruction body.
Preparation establishes validated data availability, not prompt authority, execution, or permission.
